newsitem.title: USA: Weather may force U.S. shuttle home early.
newsitem.headline: Weather may force U.S. shuttle home early.

text.p: The space shuttle Columbia may have to return to earth a day early because of a forecast for bad weather at landing sites on both U.S. coasts, NASA officials said on Tuesday.

The shuttle's mission was recently extended until on Friday, but poor weather is forecast for the shuttle's prime landing site in Florida and high winds would affect the backup landing strips in California and New Mexico, mission control's Marc Garneau told the five astronauts.
Early on Wednesday, the shuttle's five-member crew is scheduled to recapture a star-gazing telescope that has been trailing the orbiter through space for the past two weeks.

The Orfeus-Spas telescope, released from the shuttle shortly after launch, has been one of the success stories of a mission marred by a jammed airlock hatch that forced the cancellation of two planned spacewalks.

On Monday, ground controllers decided to extend the mission by a day to give the telescope, a U.S.-German project, more time to gather data on interstellar matter in a study on the life cycles of stars.
The extra day had meant that Columbia was scheduled to return to Earth on Friday, landing at Florida's Kennedy Space Center shortly after 8 a.m. EST (1300 GMT).
